text:
Career exploration · Mathematics · Statistics & Data Science



Answer five quick questions to explore a math career path that may fit your interests. Then browse salary snapshots, training ideas, and possible job titles. There are no wrong answers.








NoteExplore Math and Statistics at CSUMB



Our programs include Mathematics for Teaching, Pure & Applied Math, and Statistics & Data Science. Our programs include small classes, faculty mentorship, hands-on learning, research, and service-learning. Career paths can overlap. Use these snapshots to decide what you’d like to learn more about.

Help students build mathematical understanding, confidence, and problem-solving skills.



$85,107 median annual pay for high school teachers.



A bachelor’s degree in Mathematics followed by a credential degree is required in California (as one possible avenue). Courses in Calculus, Statistics, and Geometry as well as 45 hours of classroom experience are required for credential programs in California. All of these qualifications are met in the CSUMB Mathematics for Teaching Concentration. In addition, programs like Math and Science Teacher Initiative (MSTI) provide scholarship support to engage in activities to prepare you for the classroom. Learn more about the CSUMB Mathematics Program.

Use mathematical models and computation to understand or improve real systems and practical problems.



$113,769 median annual pay for positions such as operations research analysts, (May 2024), one career that uses applied math.



AA bachelor’s degree in mathematics, with a focus on applied classes such as modeling, numerical, and data analysis, with programming in Python and Matlab, are all skills gained through the Pure and Applied Mathematics Concentration at CSUMB. Our program provides experiential learning and research opportunities directly embedded in your courses, with additional opportunities for faculty mentored research and internships. Some specialized roles require graduate study, and we offer a special course to help you navigate the application process to Master’s and PhD programs. Learn more about the CSUMB Mathematics Program.



Applied mathematician
Operations research analyst
Computational Scientist
Quantitative analyst





Turning a practical question into equations or a computer model, testing scenarios, and explaining what a solution could mean in the context of the problem.







CSUMB student works on a problem on a white board




Study mathematical ideas for their structure, patterns, and proofs, including questions with no immediate practical use.



$114,970 median annual pay for mathematicians, but positions typically require a PhD.



A bachelor’s degree prepare students for related work in areas such as Artificial Intelligence or Cryptography. Topics may include real analysis, abstract algebra, and number theory, all courses offered as a part of the Pure and Applied Mathematics Concentration at CSUMB. Since a PhD is typically required for research mathematician jobs, students can start research experiences early through course-based experiences followed by faculty mentored research. In addition, many students find support through the Undergraduate Research Opportunities Center to find additional summer research experiences. Finally, students can complete a special course to help you navigate the application process to a PhD program. Learn more about the CSUMB Mathematics Program.



Research mathematician
University mathematics professor
Mathematical analyst
Mathematics writer or editor





Reading mathematical work, asking precise questions, developing proofs, writing results, or discussing ideas with other mathematicians.







Students and faculty work on a data analysis project.




Use data, probability, and computing to find patterns, measure uncertainty, and inform decisions.



$136,000 median annual pay for statisticians and $141,590 for data scientists.



The CSUMB Statistics & Data Science bachelor’s degree prepares you for many possible jobs in one of the fastest growing fields in the United States. The combination of both Statistics and Data Science provides you with the chance to choose your path, whether you test new treatments for diseases or use machine learning making predictions about ticket sales for a sports team. Since some roles require a master’s degree or PhD, our program mixes both theoretical foundations with computational methods so that you can easily transitions to graduate degree program. Students gain hands-on learning through course-based projects, a service-learning internship, and faculty-mentored research experiences or work as a consultant our data analysis center on campus. Learn more about the CSUMB Statistics & Data Science Program.

Data scientist

Biostatistician





Cleaning data, choosing an analysis, checking whether a pattern is reliable, and communicating what the evidence can and cannot show.

title: Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges
text: Try a short activity that gives you a glimpse of four math careers. Choose a challenge, start its five-minute timer, and finish by reflecting on what you enjoyed or want to investigate next.

title: Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges
text:
Math Teaching
Math teachers help people make sense of ideas and find ways through confusion.
Your student says: “I know 3 × 4 is 12, but I don’t understand why.” Help them see what multiplication means.

Choose a model: equal groups, an array, or a number line.
Sketch it or describe it in one or two sentences.
Ask a question that would help you check the student’s understanding.

I’ll use  4 groups of 3 objects 3 rows of 4 dots 3 jumps of 4 on a number line  Reveal a sample


Stretch for grades 9–12: A student says, “If you multiply by a fraction, the answer always gets bigger.” Write a counterexample and a question that could guide them to notice the pattern.

title: Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges
text:
Pure Math
Pure mathematicians explore patterns, structures, and why mathematical statements are true.
Explore: Look at the first few square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25… Compare each one with the square before it.

Find the differences between neighboring squares.
Predict the next difference and the next square number.
Try to explain why the differences follow that pattern.

Next difference:  Check


Stretch for grades 9–12: Use (n + 1)² − n² to explain why the differences between consecutive square numbers are consecutive odd numbers.

title: Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges
text:
Applied Math
Applied mathematicians build and use mathematical models to help answer practical questions.
Design challenge: A short ramp rises 3 feet over a horizontal run of 12 feet. The slope is rise ÷ run. Imagine making the ramp twice as long while keeping the same steepness.

Calculate the original slope.
Double the horizontal run. What rise keeps the slope the same?
What real-world details might a simple slope calculation leave out?

New rise (feet):  Check


Stretch for grades 9–12: Write the proportional relationship between rise and run. Name one assumption in this model and one additional constraint an engineer might need to consider.

title: Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges
text:
Statistics & Data Science
Statisticians and data scientists look for useful patterns while checking how data was collected and what it can tell us.
Question: How long, in minutes, did seven students take to get to school? Data: 8, 10, 10, 12, 13, 14, 45

Find the mean (average) and the median (middle value).
Which better describes a “typical” trip here? Why?
What would you want to know before drawing a conclusion about all students?

I think the more typical value is  Choose one the mean the median  Check


Stretch for grades 9–12: Calculate both values, then explain how the 45-minute trip affects them differently. Suggest one way to collect a more representative sample.
